about.title: Gardena Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a traffic collision takes someone from your family in Gardena, the grief is immediate but the legal questions often arrive later — sometimes in the middle of funeral arrangements or while sorting through bills. Los Angeles County crash records show that Gardena's busiest corridors, including Rosecrans Avenue and Normandie Avenue, see regular collision activity, and even a small number of these crashes turn fatal each year. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain circumstances. These civil claims run separately from any criminal proceedings and follow their own two-year deadline from the date of death — shorter if a government entity may be involved. We handle wrongful death claims arising from traffic collisions and can review your family's situation at no charge so you can focus on your family while we examine the legal side.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing under certain circumstances. We can review your family's situation and explain your specific rights.

items.question: How long do we have to file after losing a loved one in a Gardena crash?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. That deadline can be shorter if a government entity, like a city road authority, may share responsibility. Given that Gardena's higher-collision corridors include public roads such as Rosecrans Avenue and Western Avenue, it's worth having a claim reviewed promptly.

items.question: What kinds of losses can a wrongful death claim cover?
items.answer: These claims can potentially address funeral and burial costs, lost financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of companionship, love, and guidance. Every family's situation is different, and we can walk through what may apply to yours. No outcome or dollar amount is ever guaranteed.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case?
items.answer: No — a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, even if criminal charges are also filed against the at-fault driver. The two proceedings run independently and have different standards and outcomes. Your family can pursue a civil claim regardless of what happens in any criminal case.
